note: v1: SAY IT AGAIN, deep soulful house in B minor at 119.5 rising to 120, built on the SPEECH-TO-SONG illusion. A spoken phrase, 'Just one more step, and we're home', loops every two bars over a bare groove (kick, off-beat hats, a swung shaker, a pumped 808 holding B): it is speech, each syllable with a speaking glide, but its speaking pitches sit secretly on the tape's stair (C#3 C#3 D3 F#3, D3 C#3 B2). After sixteen repetitions the Rhodes starts doubling exactly those pitches, quietly and then fully, the chords arrive under them (Bm9 Gmaj7 Em9 F#7sus), and in the drop a soft lead sings the phrase two octaves up while the stair rises on celesta every eight bars (the thread). In the break the drums leave and the bare voice returns alone - still heard as singing - repeating every SEVEN beats so it slides against the bar. The outro thins the voice away and settles the 808 on F#, the fifth that hands to t6's F# minor. Mastered by the song's own loudness -11 (proposed for the tape), a fast compressor catching the kick before the true-peak limiter: -11.0 LUFS, true peak -1.29 dBTP, runs 2, crest 11.3; seeds 0/11: 95.25 / 95.50 (spectrum 84 and rhythm 79 the soft spots). The pitch check: the voice lands within 6-28 cents of its targets.
next: Harry's notes; spectrum 84 (find the band); the seams with t4 and t6 once they're claimed; a filter or LFO doing a job in the speech section.

note: v2: ONE LINE, TWO - recomposed. v1's speech-to-song collided with chirper-one's t3 (declared 18 seconds earlier, same illusion, nearly the same phrase), so t5 yields it and becomes MINIMAL DEEP ACID on AUDITORY STREAMING. One 303 line plays van Noorden's gallop in sixteenths, low-high-low-rest. While its notes are a tone apart (B and C#) you hear one galloping line; then the high note climbs the tape's stair (C#, D, F#, B, and on up to D and F# an octave higher) and past about half an octave the ear can't hold it as one line any more: it splits into two players, a steady eighth-note bass and a syncopated line on the 'e' of every beat, and the gallop vanishes, though not one note has moved in time. The break drops the drums, pulls the two streams apart in space (8 dB to either side) and then closes the gap a step a bar until they fuse back into one; the drop re-climbs the stair every eight bars (fuse, waver, split, again) over a root walking B G E F#, with dub stabs on the 'and' of two and four into a 3/16 delay; the outro is one line again and settles the 808 on F# for t6. Odd-length motion: the acid's filter on a seven-bar LFO, the hats' high-pass on five, the stabs' band-pass on nine. Mastered at the song's loudness -11 (true peak -1.29 dBTP, runs 2); seeds 0/11: 96.19 / 96.10 (v1 95.25), variety 96, spectrum 74 (still heavy at 44-60 Hz and short on top: next).
next: Harry's notes; the 44-60 Hz excess (kick/808) and the top end (spectrum 74); the seams once t4/t6 are claimed; maybe a second slot.

note: v3: THE SEAM, and the line comes forward. t5's kick and hats stopped two bars before its end, so its last seconds were near-silence against t6's entrance (level jump 15.7 dB); now the beat runs to the last bar, carrying the 808's F# into t6, where that F# turns phantom (the seam is t6's missing-fundamental illusion; I own both sides). And the machine-kit kick, which in t6 measured 14 dB over everything else in the low end, comes down 6 dB here too: the acid line and its split come forward and the loudness stage spends its level on the music rather than the boom (spectrum 74 -> 78). Seeds 0/11 (v2 88.90 / 88.82 rescored with t6 beside it): 90.46 / 90.48, flow 25 -> 44 (seam jump 15.7 -> 7.7 dB); levels clean (-11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, runs 1).

note: v4: THE RATE. Streaming hangs on two things, the pitch gap and the speed, and until now t5 only played the gap. In the break the two lines still pan apart at their widest (bars 81-88), then come back to the centre an octave apart - and the gallop slows to EIGHTHS: at half the rate the same wide gap no longer splits, and the ear fuses them into one slow, loping line (89-92); the gap then closes a step a bar, still in eighths, and at 97 the drop snaps back to sixteenths, where the climbing stair splits it again. Nothing changed in the pitches, only the speed: the second half of the illusion, and a half-time moment in the set. Also the top opened (master shelf +4 dB at 7 kHz; above 5 kHz was 6-12 dB short) and the kick sits 2 dB lower. Seeds 0/11 (v3 91.43 / 91.44 rescored): 91.99 / 92.03, spectrum 78 -> 85, cohesion 86 -> 93 (flow 47 -> 41: the brighter top against t6's head, which is mine to brighten); -11.1 LUFS, TP -1.29, runs 1.
